description: Verify that DUT learns IP↔MAC mappings from a *gratuitous* ARP Response (opcode 2, sender == target) — once learned, DUT must not emit its own ARP Request when sending to that IP (RFC 826 §2.3 + Linux net.ipv4.conf.<iface>.arp_accept=1)
approach:
[Objective]
Gratuitous ARP variant of ARP_03. Instead of seeding the cache with an ARP Request (opcode 1), the tester announces its presence with a gratuitous ARP Response (opcode 2) where sender == target == <HOST-1-IP, MAC-ADDR1>. A node that honours gratuitous announcements (Linux requires `net.ipv4.conf.<iface>.arp_accept=1`, set by setup-netns.sh on the DUT veth) must add the mapping just as it would from a Request, so the next packet to HOST-1-IP reuses the cached MAC without emitting a new ARP Request.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: gratuitous ARP Response injected
   • opcode      = 2
   • sender IP   = HOST-1-IP
   • sender MAC  = MAC-ADDR1
   • target IP   = HOST-1-IP   (== sender → 'gratuitous')
   • target MAC  = MAC-ADDR1
   ⇒ DUT must add <HOST-1-IP, MAC-ADDR1> to its ARP cache.

2. Tester → DUT: SOME/IP Subscribe-Nack message
   ⇒ Stimulates DUT to send a UDP response back to HOST-1-IP.

3. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: UDP packet (using the cached MAC)
   • DUT must NOT emit its own ARP Request

[Pass condition]
Within the observation window, DUT does not emit its own ARP Request — meaning the gratuitous announcement seeded the cache successfully.

[Fail condition]
Fail_unexpected_arp_request — DUT emitted an ARP Request with its own MAC as sender. Most common cause is `arp_accept=0` on the DUT iface; the kernel then ignores gratuitous announcements per RFC 5227 §1.2 default behaviour.

verdicts.Pass: DUT sent UDP using the cached MAC without an extra ARP Request — gratuitous learning worked
verdicts.Fail_unexpected_arp_request: DUT emitted its own ARP Request after the gratuitous announcement — gratuitous learning failed (likely arp_accept=0)
